layout_dets.text: •We propose a method for obtaining the relative depth

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of targets from 2D images: the pseudo-depth method,

layout_dets.text: to compare the relative depth relationships between

layout_dets.text: decomposition.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Based on the aforementioned design, we propose a new

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: IoU-only tracker named as SparseTrack, which signifi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cantly outperforms the previous IoU-only trackers and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: achieves comparable results with recent state-of-the-art

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: MOT methods on a wide range of MOT benchmarks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SparseTrack achieves impressive performance on mul-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tiple tracking datasets, which proves the effectiveness of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: target set decomposition based on pseudo-depth. We take

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ByteTrack as a baseline. On the MOT17 [3] test set, Sparse-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Track achieved 65.1 HOTA [14], 81.0 MOTA, and 80.1 IDF1,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which are gains of +2.0 HOTA, +0.7 MOTA, and +2.8

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: IDF1 compared to the baseline. On the MOT20 [4] dataset,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SparseTrack achieved 63.4 HOTA, 78.2 MOTA, and 77.3

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: IDF1, which are gains of +2.1 HOTA, +0.4 MOTA, and +2.1

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: IDF1 compared to the baseline. Furthermore, we evaluate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SparseTrack on DanceTrack [15] benchmark and obtain a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gain of +7.8 HOTA, +1.7 MOTA, +4.4 IDF1 compared to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: baseline. It is worth noting that our proposed DCM algo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rithm is plug-and-play and can be integrated into different

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trackers, resulting in consistent performance improvements.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: occlusion order is highly correlated with the depth order.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: As a result, the targets in each subset can be handled in a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fine-grained manner and be less affected by the targets in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: other depth levels.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To realize the above designs, we propose a method for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: obtaining the relative depth of targets from 2D images: the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pseudo-depth method, which is based on two scene priors:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1) the camera that captures objects is higher than the ground,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2) all objects in the scene are on flat ground. In other words,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: there are no obvious undulations on the ground. In this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: case, we can project the relative depth of targets from 3D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: space onto the 2D image plane and obtain target pseudo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: depth values, which is the distance from the bottom of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the target bounding box to the bottom edge of the image.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Notably, the pseudo-depth value is used as a reference

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to measure the relative depth relationship between targets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: using the ground as a reference system, rather than the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ground truth depth of the target in 3D space. Furthermore,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we design a depth cascade matching (DCM) algorithm to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: execute hierarchical association based on the target pseudo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: depth information. Specifically, we divide trajectories and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: detections into multiple target subsets according to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: distribution of pseudo-depth value. The DCM algorithm

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performs IoU [13] association on these sparse target subsets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the order of pseudo-depth value from nearest to farthest.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: By integrating the pseudo-depth method and DCM into the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: data association process, we propose a novel tracker called

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SparseTrack. The essence of SparseTrack lies in associating

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: occlusions hierarchically based on depth via the DCM, as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shown in Fig. 3.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.1 2D Multi-Object Tracking

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The current mainstream work on 2D multi-object tracking

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: focuses on ensuring robust temporal associations, which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can lead to the development of various tracking methods.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Based on different temporal modeling methods, current

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mainstream tracking approaches can be roughly divided

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into four categories: temporal associations via positional

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: information, temporal associations via appearance features,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: temporal associations via graph optimization, and temporal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: associations via attention mechanisms. Early trackers [5],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [16], based on deep learning perform temporal associations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: between consecutive frames via positional information and

layout_dets.text: 2.2 Methods for Handling Object Occlusion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: employ the Kalman filter [17] based on constant velocity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: motion priors to model the inter-frame motion of the targets,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which can ensure the stability of the trajectories. To achieve

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the long-term association, DeepSORT [18] and MOTDT [19]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enhance SORT [5] by adding appearance cues to compen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sate for the defect of positional information in associating

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: long-term trajectories. Although appearance cues generated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by re-identification (ReID) models [20], [21], [22], [23] are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effective for associating long-term objects, challenges are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: posed by target occlusions and motion blurs to the reli-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ability of these cues. Some methods [24], [25], [26], [27],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [28] use the ReID models enhanced by self-supervised pre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training [29], [30], [31], [32], [33] to alleviate the poor ap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pearance of occluded targets, but it comes with a higher

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: computational cost. Other trackers, such as [34], [35], [36],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improve computational efficiency by jointly optimizing the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: detection task and the re-identification task within a single

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: framework, which somewhat limits the upper bound of de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tection performance and appearance quality. Partial works

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [7], [8], [11], [12], [37] are inspired by Transformer [38],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [39], [40], [41] and attempt to implement trajectory temporal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: propagation from the perspective of attention mechanism

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and achieve impressive performance in complex scenes [15],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [42], While the computational overhead generated by self-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: attention and feed-forward networks is still non-negligible.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Although the methods [43], [44], [45], [46], [47] offer com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: putationally efficient trajectory temporal propagation based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on convolutional neural network (CNN) [48], they struggle

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with the association problem for crowded targets. Recent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: works [9], [49], [50], [51], [52], [53], formulate multiple object

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tracking as a graph optimization problem, using graph

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: neural networks or graph matching to achieve robust data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: association. However, the computational overhead based on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: graphs tends to increase square fold when the number of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: targets in the scene increases.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The performance of a tracker is to some extent dependent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on the ability to handle occlusions. Recent works have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: attempted to tackle occlusion from different perspectives.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For example, MotionTrack [54] learns the motion pattern of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trajectories and combines it with historical information to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effectively model tracks of occlusions. MOTR [11], an end-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to-end MOT framework, processes new appearing targets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and tracked targets separately using detection queries and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trajectory queries, respectively, with a multi-frame training

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: manner. Due to the relative independence among queries

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and sufficient temporal training, MOTR can perform well in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: temporal modeling of occlusions across time steps. DP-MOT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [55] proposes a subject-ordered depth estimation (SODE)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method to automatically sort the depth positions of de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tected objects in 2D scenes in an unsupervised manner. By

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: constructing a pseudo-3D Kalman filter, DP-MOT achieves

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: robust association for occluded targets. BoT-SORT [56] com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bines camera motion compensation (CMC) and IoU-ReID

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fusion, which can integrate motion and appearance clues

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the object for achieving accurate tracking of occlusions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OUTrack [28] uses an unsupervised re-identification module

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and occlusion-aware module to predict the locations where

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: target occlusions occur, in order to compensate for missed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Actually, many trackers that follow the tracking-by-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: detection paradigm perform some degree of the target set

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decomposition. For example, DeepSORT [18] achieves step-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by-step association of the detection set through multi-stage

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cascaded matching. FairMOT [35] processes the detection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: set separately based on appearance and position clues,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which can also be seen as a division of the detection set

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: via tracking clues. LMGP [59] effectively eliminates tra-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: jectory errors in single-camera trackers by introducing a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pre-clustering method driven by 3D geometric projections,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which groups detected objects for association. ByteTrack [6]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: divides the detection set into high-score and low-score de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tections based on confidence scores, and uses the correlation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: between scores and occlusions to separately process low-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: score occluded targets. However, in dense crowds, conges-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion leads to occlusions, which results in low-score detec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions. Although ByteTrack decouples low-score occlusions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from the scene, low-score targets are still crowded. In this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: case, IoU-based data association is prone to matching errors

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that limit the tracking ability to handle occlusions. To this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: end, SparseTrack divides the detection set and the trajectory

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: set based on the pseudo-depth level to ensure that targets in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: each association step are no longer crowded.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Depth information is commonly used in applications related

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to 3D scenes, such as monocular or stereo depth estimation,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3D detection and tracking, and recently popular neural

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: radiance fields [60]. The standard depth provides abundant

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: information on the appearance and position of objects, lead-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing to different 3D tracking methods. For instance, TrackR-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: 4.1.3 Implementation details

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We use the common CLEAR metrics [67] (MOTA, FP, FN,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performance. DetA is used to measure detection accuracy.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: overall effectiveness of detection and association.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: While SparseTrack demonstrates remarkable performance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improvements on both the MOT datasets and the Dance-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Track dataset, it has poor performance on the public detec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion benchmark of the MOT dataset. The association per-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formance of SparseTrack is substantially contingent on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: detector's capacity to accurately identify occluded targets.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To be precise, SparseTrack places a higher reliance on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: detection quality of partially obscured and low-confidence

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: targets compared to conventional detection-based tracking

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods. In addition, SparseTrack faces challenges in other

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: demanding scenarios such as [82], [83] where targets exhibit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rapid motion and deformation. In such cases, it becomes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: difficult for the pseudo-depth method to capture the relative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: depth relationships accurately, which affects the tracking

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performance of SparseTrack. For videos with low frame

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Compared to previous methods that rely on position

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: information and Kalman filter [17], the association approach

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of SparseTrack achieves the best tracking performance on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the aforementioned three validation sets.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the performance of associating crowded targets intuitively,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shown in Fig. 7, Fig. 8 and Fig. 9, respectively.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We propose a simple tracker for multi-object tracking named

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as SparseTrack. It leverages the pseudo-depth method to es-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: timate the relative depth relationship between different tar-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gets and divides the target set into multiple sparse subsets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in order of increasing depth. In order to associate occluded

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: targets distributed across these sparse subsets, we introduce

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the Depth Cascade Matching (DCM) algorithm, which per-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: forms the association between detection subsets and trajec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tory subsets at the same depth level. Compared to previous

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tracking methods, SparseTrack offers a different perspec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tive on addressing occlusion: the target set decomposition,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which partitions the dense target set into sparse subsets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by pseudo-depth information. SparseTrack achieves com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: petitive performance on the MOT17 and MOT20 datasets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: comparing to state-of-the-art methods via solely utilizing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: simple IoU distance association, without relying on robust

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: appearance embeddings or enhanced motion prediction.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This demonstrates the effectiveness of decomposition based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on depth information. It is worth noting that DCM is plug-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and-play and can be integrated into any existing tracker,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: yielding consistent performance improvements. We hope

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that SparseTrack can provide alternative solutions for multi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: object tracking tasks and inspire the development of more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: powerful and elegant approaches based on the concept of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sparsity in the future.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Comparing to ByteTrack, SparseTrack demonstrates greater

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stability in handling challenging occlusion scenarios. It is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: attributed to its ability to differentiate between targets at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: various depths crowded together, leveraging discriminative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pseudo-depth information originating from the targets.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Visualization of the target set decomposition. Although

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the target set decomposition is a sub-process of DCM, it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is the key to decoupling dense occlusions. In fact, not all

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: targets in the scene are occluded state, but occluded targets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: may gather together and form dense occlusions easier, as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on pseudo-depth information, overlapping targets can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: assigned to different depth levels, effectively. We visualize
